about: What `tur-diag heal notices --json` prints, under `printed`: an array of the notices this person has not seen, each with id, at_utc, code, kind, title, body and actions (services/tur-diagnostics/src/heal/engine.rs, struct Notice; the healing service's engineer declared these fields stable on 14 November 2026: fields may be added, never renamed). WRITTEN BY HAND from that struct and from the texts of services/tur-diagnostics/heal/catalogue.json with their subjects filled in; not recorded from a run of tur-diag. The fourth notice carries the longer text pull request #117 gives an automatic repair. Recording this file in the heal workflow, as tur-pax-ui's fixture is recorded from the real service, is a follow-up (docs/reports/desktop-8.md).

printed.title: A system service stopped working
printed.body: chronyd.service had stopped working. TUR started it again and checked that it is running.

printed.title: Name lookups bypass the system resolver
printed.body: Name lookups bypass the system resolver: /etc/resolv.conf was replaced. If you did not mean this, TUR can restore it, and undo that later.

printed.title: A TUR program crashed
printed.body: tur-diag crashed. This is a problem in TUR itself. You can send a report to TUR's developers; you see everything in it first, and nothing is sent unless you choose to.

printed.title: A system service stopped working
printed.body: cups.service had stopped working. TUR started it again and checked that it is running. TUR did this by itself; it checks again at its next look and tells you whether the repair held.
